instruction:
SliceCurve + Panel Loops on a Helmet Dome

The file at C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named Helmet, is a dome-shaped upper hemisphere of radius 1 BU centred at origin (y in [0, 1]), tessellated at 12 latitude rings x 24 longitude columns = 288 quads plus 24 triangles at the apex. Its faces are pre-assigned to six longitudinal polygroups named Panel_1..Panel_6, each covering a 60-degree wedge of longitude. The SubTool has no UVs, no polypaint, and no subdivision levels.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush, use SliceCurve to cut the helmet along the six polygroup boundaries, run Panel Loops to extrude each panel into a thick manifold shell with a beveled outer edge, split the result into six independent SubTools named Panel_1..Panel_6, and export the result as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj.

The exported C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj must satisfy:

- Exactly six SubTools, named Panel_1 through Panel_6.
- Each SubTool is a closed manifold mesh.
- Each SubTool's longitudinal angular span is in [50, 70] degrees.
- The total face count across all six panels is in [400, 900].
- A beveled outer rim is present: across all panels there are at least 10 short chamfer edges, and their mean length is less than 0.025 BU.
